description: lib.rs:2109-2124: matched_via_i uses .fold(false, |_, _parent| { new_nodes.push(...); true }). This is a side-effecting fold: the accumulator is discarded, new_nodes is mutated as a side effect of the iteration, and the result is just 'was the iterator non-empty?'. The Rust idiomatic form is: 'let mut matched_via_i = false; for parent in tree.iter().filter(...) { matched_via_i = true; new_nodes.push(...); }'. The fold form is both unidiomatic and confusing — it obscures that (a) the iterator is consumed twice conceptually (once for flag, once for push) and (b) the accumulator is intentionally discarded.
title: pkix-path (rusty): fold-with-side-effect in policy tree d(1)(i) — use for-loop + flag
